name: lanka-monorepo
description: The lanka framework monorepo: core, modules, plugins, tools.

scripts.//scaffold: Package manifests and documentation are derived from scripts/registry.mjs. Edit the registry and regenerate: a direct edit to a package.json is overwritten, deliberately.
scripts.//check:drift: Generated output against the registry. A hand edit does not survive the next scaffold run; this check finds it before the divergence ships to npm.
scripts.//check:naming: Names: directories, files, symbols, config keys. Canon is skills/naming/SKILL.md; a rule nothing fails on diverges from the code silently.
scripts.//check:router: CLAUDE.md is AGENTS.md plus a header. One router, one wording; --write regenerates it.
scripts.//check:publishable: Publish readiness: name, version, license, repository address, private cleared. Separate from the build because the window to unpublish is 72 hours and there is no second one.
scripts.//release: Publishes every package to npm, by hand. The order is the point: the generated output against the registry, then the whole chain, then the packages — so a manual release cannot skip what CI used to run for it. Add --otp=<code> when the account has 2FA.
scripts.release: pnpm run check && pnpm -r publish --access public
scripts.//lint: Run through `node` with a raised heap rather than through the `eslint` bin: the default limit is reached on this repository now, and eslint reports it as an abort with a V8 stack rather than as a lint failure — the kind of red a contributor reads as a broken machine. Invoking node directly keeps the flag portable, which `NODE_OPTIONS=` in a script is not on Windows.
scripts.//check:playgrounds: Six applications written by hand drift the way six hand-written suites would. Holds each to the scene list its contract names, and Astro to one island per binding.
scripts.//test: Sequential, deliberately — and ENFORCED, not just described. Each vitest already fans out across every core, so several packages at once thrash rather than share: --parallel failed three of seven runs here, in a different package each time and always with "Failed to terminate worker" rather than an assertion, and the same run under coverage died with "JavaScript heap out of memory" in whichever package was fourth in line. Sequential passed three of three at the same wall time — 35-43s either way. pnpm -r is NOT sequential by default (workspace-concurrency 4), so the flag is what makes this sentence true.
scripts.//check: The whole list is `.specwarden/checks/`, and this runs all of it: the fast tier first, so a canon divergence is reported before the suites start, then the heavy one. CI calls this same command. Every check has a rule and a proof that it looked; `specwarden check --list` prints them in order, `specwarden check <id>` runs one. The tree must be clean for `drift`, which `check` on a commit already is.
scripts.check: specwarden check --all --tier fast && specwarden check --all --tier heavy
scripts.//doctor: What the list declares, without running any of it: every check, its tier and capabilities, and which rule each one holds.
scripts.//check:structure: What shares a file, what a barrel holds, where a test lives. Canon is skills/structure/SKILL.md; a rule nothing falls from diverges from the code silently.
scripts.//check:composition: Function length, repeated blocks, branch shape. Canon is skills/composition/SKILL.md; the budgets are a ratchet that may only fall.
scripts.//test:scripts: The repository guard scripts. They are not workspace packages, so pnpm -r does not run them.
scripts.//check:family: The validator family: every package binding ILankaValidator publishes one surface, differing only in the vendor name. It was a hard-coded PAIR, which stopped being true at the third validator.
scripts.//check:forms: The form every published thing takes: class, factory, frozen table, ambient instance. Canon is skills/forms/SKILL.md.
scripts.//check:parity: Every role written in both styles over one implementation. Canon is skills/parity/SKILL.md.
scripts.//check:llms: The machine-readable half: llms.txt and the skill marketplace. Nobody here reads either, which is why they rot — a dead link is invisible to us and total for the model or the person who followed it.
scripts.//check:runtime: Where each package runs — browser, node, native — against what its sources actually require. Canon is skills/hosts/SKILL.md; an undeclared environment is a consumer guessing.
scripts.//check:perf: The hot paths against the recorded baseline. NOT in `check`: every other gate reads files and answers the same on any machine, while this one measures and needs an instrument — on a busy laptop or a two-core runner everything regresses together, controls included. Run it deliberately on an idle machine; :write records there, :report prints without judging and is what CI runs.
scripts.//bench: Every package's benches, printed rather than compared — for reading numbers while optimising.
